common_name: Kilburn Rose Dahlia (Soft Pink-Peach Waterlily Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Kilburn Rose carries shallow, waterlily-form blooms in soft blended pink and peach, with broad flat petals that curve gently upward like a floating lily flower rather than the deep, fully double shape of decorative types. The open form sheds rain well and holds its shape nicely in arrangements. Pinch the growing tip early to encourage branching and a fuller flush of blooms. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Taratahi Ruby Dahlia (Deep Red Waterlily Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Taratahi Ruby bears shallow, flat-faced waterlily-form blooms in a rich, saturated red, giving a cleaner and more open look than fully double cactus or decorative types in the same color range. The sparse petal count means blooms open quickly and hold their color well in heat. Stake stems in exposed sites since the flowers sit on relatively slender stalks. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Ryecroft Marge is an anemone-flowered dahlia, with a single outer ring of pink ray florets surrounding a dense, pincushion-like center of shorter tubular yellow florets, a distinctive two-tier look unlike any ball or decorative type. The flat outer petals help pollinators reach the central disc. Deadhead regularly to keep the compact plants flowering through the season. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Freya's Paso Doble Dahlia (White-and-Yellow Anemone-Flowered Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Freya's Paso Doble shows the characteristic anemone form, a single flat ring of white outer petals framing a raised, tightly packed cushion of yellow tubular florets at the center. The contrast between the flat outer collar and domed center gives it a distinct texture in mixed plantings compared to fully double dahlia forms. Pinch young plants to promote branching and more flowering stems. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Honka is a single orchid-type dahlia with narrow, pointed golden-yellow petals that curl slightly along their edges, giving each bloom a spidery, star-like silhouette very different from the broad, flat rays of standard single dahlias. The airy, open flowers are produced in abundance and read almost like a species dahlia in the border. Its fine-textured foliage and wiry stems also make it a graceful filler in cut arrangements. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Mayan Pearl Dahlia (Pink Double Orchid-Flowered Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Mayan Pearl is a double orchid-flowered dahlia, meaning its narrow, involute (inward-curled) pink petals form multiple overlapping layers rather than the single ring seen on standard orchid types, giving a fuller, more layered star shape. The slender petals give the whole flower a lighter, lacier look than ball or decorative dahlias of similar size. Deadhead spent blooms promptly to keep new buds coming. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Mary's Jomanda Dahlia (Pink-and-Purple Miniature Ball Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Mary's Jomanda produces small, tightly spiraled ball-form blooms blending pink and purple tones, a sport of the better-known orange ball dahlia 'Jomanda' but distinct in color. The neat, perfectly rounded flowers are a favorite for cutting because the compact heads hold their globe shape well in the vase. Disbud to encourage larger, more uniform balls, or leave the plant unthinned for a prolific flush of smaller blooms. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost.

directions: Josie Gott carries densely packed, spherical ball blooms in white brushed and flecked with purple, the tightly spiraled florets giving each flower a crisp, geometric roundness. The firm, long-lasting blooms are well suited to cutting and hold their form for days once cut. Stake the upright stems in windy spots to keep the round flower heads from flopping. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Gallery Art Nouveau Dahlia (Raspberry-Pink Dwarf Container Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 3-4 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost; well suited to large pots.

directions: Gallery Art Nouveau is part of the dwarf Gallery series bred specifically for container growing, staying compact and well-branched while producing fully double decorative blooms in a saturated raspberry pink. Its short, sturdy stems mean it rarely needs staking even in pots on a windy patio. Deadhead regularly to keep the naturally bushy plants flowering continuously through summer. Tubers can be lifted and stored over winter in zones colder than 8, or the small tubers grown as annuals.

common_name: Gallery Vincent Dahlia (Yellow-and-Orange Dwarf Container Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 3-4 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost; well suited to large pots.

directions: Gallery Vincent is a dwarf, container-bred dahlia from the Gallery series, carrying warm yellow-to-orange double blooms on a low, naturally bushy plant that needs little support. The compact habit and continuous bloom make it a reliable choice for patio pots and small border edges alike. Pinch the center growing tip early on to encourage more branching and a fuller shape. Tubers can be lifted and stored over winter in zones colder than 8, or the small tubers grown as annuals.
